title: Choose the owning process before the database file
description: Combine a query shape, connection boundary, mutation pattern, and storage path. The result shows whether DuckDB owns the workload cleanly or should remain a downstream analytics engine.

workloads.label: Notebook exploration
workloads.detail: One analyst scans bounded files and iterates on analytical SQL.
workloads.guidance: Keep the connection local, pin the environment, and publish any result that others depend on.

workloads.label: Scheduled analytics job
workloads.detail: A controlled worker reads a snapshot and produces a validated data product.
workloads.guidance: Use one owned process, explicit resource settings, staging output, and atomic promotion.

workloads.label: Interactive dashboard
workloads.detail: Users expect repeated analytical reads with a bounded response-time objective.
workloads.guidance: Reuse connections, cap concurrent work, precompute expensive paths, and isolate long queries.

workloads.label: Transactional request API
workloads.detail: Many short requests create and update individual business records.
workloads.guidance: Place authoritative transactions in a client-server OLTP system and export analytical snapshots to DuckDB.

ownerships.label: One job process
ownerships.detail: One process owns lifecycle, writes, retries, and publication.
ownerships.guidance: This matches DuckDB's embedded ownership model.

ownerships.label: One backend service
ownerships.detail: A service embeds DuckDB and mediates every request.
ownerships.guidance: Bound the queue and keep one service deployment responsible for the writable database.

ownerships.label: Many read-only processes
ownerships.detail: Independent processes open the same persistent database without writers.
ownerships.guidance: Read-only access is possible, but memory, cache, file locking, and refresh strategy remain per-process concerns.

ownerships.label: Many writer processes
ownerships.detail: Separate services expect to update the native database file directly.
ownerships.guidance: Move the shared write contract to a server or catalog architecture designed for multi-process coordination.

mutations.label: Immutable snapshots
mutations.detail: Each run reads versioned files and writes a new result.
mutations.guidance: Record the input manifest and promote the validated output.

mutations.label: Append in batches
mutations.detail: One owning process appends a bounded set of rows per run.
mutations.guidance: Use transactions, verify counts, and make retry identity explicit.

mutations.label: Periodic full rebuild
mutations.detail: A new table or file version replaces the previous analytical snapshot.
mutations.guidance: Build beside the active version, validate, then swap the publication pointer.

mutations.label: High-frequency row churn
mutations.detail: Requests continuously update or delete individual rows.
mutations.guidance: Keep row-oriented operational state in an OLTP system and analyze exported changes or snapshots.

storagePaths.label: Local SSD and local temp
storagePaths.detail: The database and spill path use fast storage attached to the owning process.
storagePaths.guidance: Monitor capacity and preserve published outputs outside the worker's ephemeral disk.

storagePaths.label: Remote Parquet source
storagePaths.detail: The engine reads columnar objects over HTTP or object storage.
storagePaths.guidance: Project columns, filter early, avoid tiny files, and inspect transferred bytes.

storagePaths.label: Shared network database file
storagePaths.detail: Multiple hosts open a native database file through network-attached storage.
storagePaths.guidance: Avoid making a network-shared file the coordination protocol; use an explicit service or supported catalog boundary.

notice: The fit score is a design prompt, not a support matrix. Confirm behavior against the DuckDB version, client library, storage system, and deployment topology you actually run.
